independence: Prompts declared after implementation, before live evaluation, authored by the implementing agent. Unseen by the selector, not an independent human benchmark. Only each prompt is sent; expected answers and other cases are never included in the API payload.

cases.prompt: Build a wired barometric-pressure controller using the standard board-family option.
For my BMP280 controller I need a 400 kHz I2C bus, with the usual family operating limits.
Select the version that reduces I2C pull-up current. I do not mean reducing whole-board power or running on a battery.
I want a pressure controller at 100 kHz with a declared total bus capacitance of 150 pF; retain the fixed family power and connectors.
Pick the faster-bus variant of the pressure board. Use the profile's 100 pF total loading limit and its standard supply envelope.
Make the ESP32 pressure board with 10-kilohm SDA and SCL pull-ups at 100 kHz. All other requirements are the published family defaults.
Use 4.7k pull-ups for the wired BMP280 design. It will operate from 10 to 35 degrees C within the standard family electrical envelope.
Configure the existing pressure-controller family for an I2C clock of 400000 Hz. Keep its supported footprint, outline and regulated input.
I only want to save current in the I2C pull-up resistors: choose the low_current profile with 50 pF total bus loading, using the family defaults elsewhere.
Give me the basic pressure controller for a nominal 3.3-volt source, using standard 100-kHz I2C and a 200-pF total bus-capacitance bound.
Power this pressure controller directly from a 5 V USB port and provide a USB data connection.
The board must measure both humidity and pressure, with a dedicated humidity sensor on the PCB.
I need a qualified wireless pressure node that transmits readings over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
Create the pressure controller as a 60 by 40 mm four-layer board with an output relay for a motor.
I am deciding between the fast and low-current bus versions of the pressure board. Neither priority has been chosen yet.
I want a low-power pressure-controller node. Choose the electrical option that saves the power I care about.
